criterion: Weil positivity criterion; the precise admissible domain, normalization and topology must be formalized before an extension claim is made.

claims.statement: Finite Gaussian-cosine Weil Gram computations supply only approximate diagnostic values.
claims.topology: Finite-dimensional Euclidean parameter spans; not the full LF test space.
claims.assumptions: Numerical quadrature and finite prime-power cutoff have unbounded total rigorous error.
claims.discharge: Independent interval arithmetic with rigorous cutoffs would certify individual finite cases only.

claims.statement: Precisely specified compactly supported smooth test functions with chosen symmetries are dense in the exact admissible Weil-criterion test domain.
claims.topology: UNRESOLVED: define the LF inductive-limit topology and the topology used for the target domain; these are not interchangeable.
claims.assumptions: A precise underlying space, inclusion map, test-function normalization and approximation mode must be fixed.
claims.discharge: Provide a rigorous density theorem including topology and admissible approximation nets or sequences.

claims.statement: Approximation preserves all test-space conditions required by the chosen Weil positivity criterion.
claims.topology: UNRESOLVED: topology must control the needed symmetry, support and positive-cone constraints.
claims.assumptions: The exact test-function involution and support restrictions must be fixed.
claims.discharge: Prove compatible approximation while preserving the actual admissibility constraints, or exhibit an obstruction.

claims.statement: The Weil quadratic form admits a justified positivity-preserving limiting argument along the chosen admissible approximants.
claims.topology: UNRESOLVED: require actual continuity, upper semicontinuity, or an equivalent negative-witness theorem in the relevant topology; lower semicontinuity alone is insufficient.
claims.assumptions: No continuity follows merely from abstract density.
claims.discharge: Prove continuity or the correct upper-semicontinuity/sign-stability implication for the exact Weil quadratic form. Lower semicontinuity alone fails.

claims.statement: The infinite arithmetic terms and relevant support restrictions can be controlled uniformly along the admissible approximations.
claims.topology: UNRESOLVED: specify support growth and seminorm control needed by the explicit formula.
claims.assumptions: Finite prime cutoffs and floating quadrature are insufficient for global arithmetic control.
claims.discharge: Prove quantitative prime-power and archimedean tail bounds uniform in the required approximation regime.

claims.statement: Assuming G1-G4 and G5P, transfer nonnegativity of the actual Weil form from the entire dense admissible family to the whole Weil-criterion domain.
claims.topology: UNRESOLVED: prove continuity compatibility between family and full test-space topology.
claims.assumptions: All G1-G4 hypotheses and separately established G5P are unproved; finite experiments cannot establish G5P.
claims.discharge: Provide exact analytic transfer with correct topology and sign stability; separately establish G5P.

claims.statement: An independent trusted kernel checks a complete formalization of all prerequisites and the final RH-equivalent implication.
claims.topology: Must match the exact topology specified and used by G1-G5.
claims.assumptions: A green metadata CI run is NOT kernel certification or mathematical peer review.
claims.discharge: Integrate a trusted proof assistant, pin dependencies, audit axioms and theorem statements, and obtain independent review.

claims.statement: The Weil quadratic form is nonnegative on EVERY test in the chosen fully admissible compact-bump family, not just a finite numerical basis.
claims.topology: The exact domain, involution, and topology specified by G1-G3; finite basis spans are not sufficient.
claims.assumptions: The Weil form and infinite arithmetic terms are well-defined on the entire family. Numerical eigenvalues and finite prime cutoffs do not establish this.
claims.discharge: Prove a uniform analytic nonnegativity theorem for all admissible compact bumps, or find a negative witness.
